soiling himself because he could not get to the bathroom. He 
lives alone, and called EMS to bring him in. He has no urinary 
symptoms, and only urinated on himself because he could not get 
to the toilet.

He takes Baclofen 20 mg tid and Tizanidine 2 mg tid for severe 
spasticity. He was on interferon therapy but stopped over a year

Brief Hospital Course:
1. Secondary Progressive MS:  The patient is a ___ 
right-handed man with a history of SPMS and cervical spondylosis 
s/p C5-C7 laminectomies who presented with inability to walk, 
which had worsened the few days prior to admission. His 
neurologic exam was notable for severe spasticity with only mild 
weakness, as well as hyperreflexia and loss of proprioception. 
MR ___ was limited by patient motion, but there was no overt 
cord compression due to disc or vertebral abnormality. He likely 
had an MS flare in the setting of UTI and dehydration. He was 
started on Solumedrol 1 gm IV daily. His Tizanidine was 
increased to 4 mg tid. He was continued on Oxybutynin and 
Baclofen.

2. Urinary Tract Infection: The patient takes Bactrim DS daily 
for UTI prophylaxis. Urine culture grew Enterococcus, and he was 
started on Ampicillin 1g Q6 hours IV. Last four doses should be 
given on ___. Pre-renal Azotemia: His Cr was increased to 1.4 on admission, 
and FeNa was found to be 0.45%. He was given IVF with 
improvement in his creatinine.

4. During this admission a drop in the hematocrit numbers was 
noted. The likely source was the hematoma in the posterior thigh 
and IV fluids ressuscitation. Guaiac was negative, UA negative. 
Currently stable

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with worsening MS symptoms and cough.  Evaluate
for pneumonia.

___.

CHEST, AP UPRIGHT AND LATERAL VIEWS: The lungs are clear without evidence of
focal consolidation, pneumothorax or pleural effusion.  A calcified granuloma
in the right lower lobe is unchanged from prior.  The cardiomediastinal
silhouette and hilar contour are unchanged from prior.  The patient is status
post anterior cervical fusion with a plate and several screws noted.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic abnormality or significant change from
prior.

CERVICAL SPINE MRI SCAN

HISTORY:  ___ man with multiple sclerosis and prior cervical
laminectomies.  Presents with severe myelopathy.

TECHNIQUE:  Only T2 sagittal and FLAIR images could be obtained, as the
technician noted that the "patient was unable to control spasms in the legs
and did not want to continue at this time."

COMPARISON STUDY ON PACS ARCHIVE:  ___ MRI scan of the cervical
spine.

FINDINGS:  The available sagittal FLAIR images are nearly uninterpretable due
to patient motion.  The sagittal T2-weighted scans are of somewhat better
quality. Given this very limited imaging, there is no overt cord compression
due to disc or vertebral abnormality.  Artifacts are noted arising from metal
screws and an anterior metallic fixation plate at the C5 through C7 levels,
also noted on the prior study. There is no gross malalignment. On the basis of
this limited study and the prior examination, there does not appear to be
evidence for prior laminectomies, as stated in your history.

CONCLUSION:  Very limited study, as noted above.

INDICATION:  ___ with hematocrit drop.

COMPARISON:  None.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
without IV or oral contrast.  Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN: Other than to note a 6-mm granuloma in the right lower lobe, the
lung bases are clear.  Heart size is normal. There is no pleural or
pericardial effusion.

On this non-contrast enhanced examination, the liver, spleen, adrenals,
kidneys, pancreas and gallbladder are unremarkable.  The intra-abdominal loops
of large and small bowel are unremarkable without evidence of pneumatosis,
free air or obstruction.  Scattered mesenteric nodes which do not meet CT size
criteria for enlargement.

CT PELVIS:  The rectum, prostate, and bladder are grossly unremarkable.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Fat containing right inguinal hernia
and surgical clips overlying the left groin are noted.

Bone windows demonstrate no evidence of lesion that is suspicious for
metastasis or infection.  Anterior wedging at T11 is noted.
 
IMPRESSION:  No acute intra-abdominal process and no evidence of abdominal
hematoma or hemorrhage.
